newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan prices to ease, focus on spot expiry.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan prices to ease, focus on spot expiry.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets are likely to tread easier this week, with market attention centring on the spot expiry session on Tuesday, traders said on Monday.
Market players were watching to see the number of deliveries at the expiry session, which could provide direction to the markets, the traders said.

"The general consensus in the markets is that there will not be a large number of deliveries at the expiry, as the current low prices will not be attractive for traders to deliver rubber," an analyst at a commodity broker said.

"But the question is whether market players will take deliveries. Given the backwardation between the March contract and the April contract, market players may postpone accepting deliveries until next month," the analyst said.
Traders said the spot March contract could tumble at the expiry if there are not many players to take deliveries.
The benchmark August contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the Monday morning session at 151.8 yen per kg, against 152.9 yen last Friday.
Similarly, the benchmark August contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 152.0 yen per kg in the second morning session, compared with 152.7 yen last Friday.

Traders said overall market sentiment was basically bearish, as fragile rubber demand from the United States and European countries, especially for technically specified rubber (TSR), and the yen's firmer trend against the dollar cast a shadow on market sentiment in Japan.

"Amid recent thin interest in rubber futures, rubber prices are vulnerable to the downside risks. The TOCOM benchmark August rubber futures contract may probe the downside at 150 yen per kg, depending on the results of the expiry," another commodity broker said.

The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted lower at 124 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis, against 125.5 cents on March 17, depressed by weaker prices in Japan and rubber producing countries.
Traders said a perception that Japan's rubber inventories will start climbing again later this month was also considered to be a negative factor for the markets.

Open interest of rubber futures in TOCOM has fallen in recent months as static prices thinned market volume. Open interest in TOCOM's rubber futures dipped to 149,999 lots as of March 21, the lowest level since October 1993.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end-users was quoted at 170 per kg on Monday compared with 169 yen on March 17.
